2) The number of points on the wings of the ladybird is equal to the number of petals on the flower. Which of the following flowers is without a ladybird?

method.method_draft: First read the top row of the image and count, for each ladybird, the black spots on the two red wings separately. For each ladybird compute its signature: (total spots on both wings, absolute difference between the two wing spot counts). Then read the bottom row and count for each labeled flower A-E: the number of red petals and the number of green leaves on its stem. Give each flower the signature (petals, leaves). Use the text rules as the matching rule: a ladybird can sit on a flower exactly when the two signatures are equal. After matching the counted ladybird signatures to the flower signatures, flowers A, B, C, and D each have at least one compatible ladybird, while flower E has 5 petals and 2 leaves and no compatible ladybird signature. Therefore the flower without a ladybird is E.

method.method_draft: Use a parity shortcut instead of fully matching every ladybird. From the bottom image, count the petals and leaves for each flower. Flower E has 5 petals and 2 leaves. From the text rules, if a ladybird has x spots on one wing and y spots on the other, then the flower would need x+y petals and |x-y| leaves. The sum x+y and the difference |x-y| always have the same parity: both even or both odd. Thus a flower with an odd number of petals and an even number of leaves cannot possibly hold any ladybird. Flower E has odd petals, 5, but even leaves, 2, so it is impossible. The other flowers are parity-compatible and can be checked visually against the available ladybirds if desired. Hence the flower without a ladybird is E.
method.CoT_raw:
Image description first: The attached picture has a top row with five ladybirds. Below it is a row of labelled flowers A, B, C, D, and E. On flower E, I can count 5 red petals and 2 green leaves on the stem.

Reasoning: If a ladybird has x spots on one wing and y spots on the other wing, then the matching flower must have x + y petals and |x - y| leaves. The numbers x + y and |x - y| always have the same parity, because adding and subtracting the same two integers gives results that are either both even or both odd. Therefore, any valid flower must have petals and leaves with the same parity. Flower E has 5 petals, which is odd, and 2 leaves, which is even. Since the parities do not match, no ladybird can sit on flower E under the rules. So the flower without a ladybird is E.
